request.topic: How TubeForge keeps captions in sync with a portrait Short
request.angle: Explain the word-to-WAV alignment, highlighted current word, portrait safe-area checks, and three-second pacing gates as TubeForge implementation details. Do not present them as universal YouTube rules.

sources.title: TubeForge README: YouTube Shorts workflow
sources.excerpt: Shorts previews are rendered at 540×960. Approved finals are rendered at 1080×1920, 30 fps with H.264 video and AAC audio. The production profile uses the original local waveform aligner to place approved words within each generated WAV; those word positions are estimates, and an independent encoded audio audit found they do not yet meet the planned timing target. The experimental `whisper-base-en-dtw-v1` provider requires a locally pinned English model and the optional `alignment` package; it aligns the approved transcript to actual speech and blocks collapsed or ambiguous boundaries. It is not installed or enabled in the production image while its one-scene gate is unverified. The experimental provider records each full alignment execution against the exact script, narration and model identity. Decode timeouts and transient model execution faults enter the worker's lease-free retry queue with 30/60/120-second backoff. If the approved tokens match but the primary alignment collapses a word to zero duration, one predefined `normalized-overlap-v1` configuration is immediately eligible on the same script/audio/model. It normalizes Unicode apostrophes in the alignment prompt and extends measured clause windows by 0.35 seconds; the approved display words never change. At most three executions per configuration and four overall are recorded. The immediate switch does not advance the transient-failure backoff count: its first later recoverable fault waits 30 seconds. This special schedule applies only during voice alignment. Invalid audio, missing model files, token ambiguity and a failed alternate block without estimated-timing substitution. Studio shows scheduled retries with the next attempt time; exhausted attempts remain failed and cannot produce an approved final. This alternate mapped one isolated accepted Git phrase, but the optional provider remains disabled until independent word timing and a full-job gate pass. The final quality gate checks structural alignment against the assembled audio, rejects a first word after three seconds, rejects visual holds over three seconds, and validates portrait caption margins and line widths. Shorts use large uppercase ASS captions near the lower-middle safe area, anchored at x=490 with a 470 px bottom margin to clear the action rail and bottom controls. The currently spoken word is yellow and surrounding words remain white. Scene holds are deterministically divided into shorter camera moves, so a long narration scene does not become one static shot. Source-grounded production writing, the fixed portrait visual system, and licensed music decisions are recorded in [`docs/SHORTS_WORKFLOW.md`](docs/SHORTS_WORKFLOW.md).
